title: Prove an all-length radical pencil obstruction for any role count
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with finite corroboration. In the paid alphabet I+u v^T on n roles, with u over R=K[x,y]/(x,y)^2, v over K and arbitrary free GL_n(K) maps:

```text
A has no K-valued left eigenvector
    => xI+yA is unreachable at every finite paid length.
```

The proof follows the first zero scalar prefix and shows that an invertible radical coefficient forces a common row for the two coefficient matrices. Later factors preserve that restriction. This extends the two-role square-zero direction of #4745 to a necessary condition at every role count. It does not recheck that predecessor or claim a converse.

The binary three-role companion of t^3+t+1 gives an explicit excluded target. Exactly 48 of the 512 binary three-by-three matrices have no scalar left eigenvector; all 48 corresponding pencils are excluded by the theorem. This is not the complete unreachable-pencil count. No new kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change.

Only `research/multirole-radical-pencil/` is added. This package was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Nick Petalas #4745 for the two-role square-zero theorem and first-zero idea, #4243 for the free-map normal form, Wentao Li #4099 following #2513 for the alphabet, and ToikY #4334 and Nick Petalas #4276/#4601/#4749 for the related two-role successors. No predecessor code is imported; the proof and verifier are self-contained.

## Evidence

- Before: #4745 classifies two-role square-zero radical targets and explicitly excludes more roles from its scope. After: the written proof gives the displayed arbitrary-field, arbitrary-length necessary condition at every role count.
- All 196 compatible binary first-zero scalar pairs pass all 802,816 single-coefficient transition checks. Exactly 150,528 have an invertible new coefficient, and every one has a nonzero common-row multiplier.
- Direct enumeration of all 512 binary three-by-three A gives 48 excluded pencils. All 168 free conjugations of the displayed companion preserve the obstruction and give 24 distinct conjugates.
- Three legal reachable controls pass 1,536 chronological comparisons on all dirty ring inputs. They distinguish a rootful triangular pencil, a singular first coefficient, and identified radical variables. Two further controls detect reversed chronology and an omitted radical contribution.
- Both warning-strict registered commands passed locally on CPython 3.12, timed separately at 0.318 s and 0.319 s. The registered package runner, five-file committed-byte/source-history preflight, official committed export and export-integrity check pass at `f5d0f421efec55c5f4b3dbb142eee1e79a4e21db`. Optimized Git-free replay passes in 0.330 s. All three generated receipts agree completely and bind all five package files by SHA256.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal claim is the written scoped proof. Executed corroboration is binary and three-role. A scalar eigenvalue is not proved sufficient. Two independent square-zero radical generators, base-field right vectors and base-field free maps are essential hypotheses. Restored auxiliary roles, ring-valued free maps and higher nilpotency are not covered. No native preparation, routing, restoration, precision, stock or complete supplier cost is supplied. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker and selected operator replay were not run; every registered package command ran locally.

## Open next questions

- Is an eigenvalue sufficient for reachability when n>=3? Start with the binary direct sum of a scalar block and the companion of t^2+t+1. The missing step is a recursive condition on the common row's quotient.
- Can a restored auxiliary role make the excluded cubic pencil reachable? Start with diag(xI_3+yA,I_1). Its nonzero scalar endpoint is outside the first-zero proof.

## Related open work

- #4745, head `3edea13af13b755932852e9306a714b317630dda`, supplies the two-role square-zero theorem and the first-zero idea. Our executed three-role census and its two-role census are disjoint; the reported 48 excluded pencils and its 12 unreachable radical targets are different quantities. No shared numerical total is claimed or rechecked.
- #4766, head `5af823b1a14b2517235925145e36581bfdfcad41`, counts all two-role radical targets over every finite field. We give a multi-role necessary condition and execute only three-role pencils, so no numeric census overlaps.
- #4764, head `b1b163cd5553c75c9bd5ca3ac31a2eab4e2f3511`, has a cost-three two-role target in a cube-zero ambient algebra. Our ring kills all radical products and our executed targets have three roles. Its exact cost and our unreachable-pencil count do not overlap.
- #4770, head `39ef149ba3ea8adbda18478ea227d3d0826475ab`, counts two-role lifts of nonzero rank-one residue matrices. Our targets have zero scalar residue, so the target domains and numerical totals are disjoint.
- #4749, head `29e4d3a25225a219f97c3a2815ed3a5a8fd9b891`, studies invertible semilocal targets. These are disjoint from our zero-residue radical targets; no cost histogram or census total overlaps.
- #4763 studies invertible two-role targets over F2[t]. Its nonsemilocal coefficient ring and endpoints differ from the square-zero radical pencils here; no numerical claim overlaps.
